title: UNWOVEN
author: Ensemble
question: When famine is declared only where data can be gathered, what does the record write for the places no one could reach, and how much of that blank did the cuts to aid and monitoring make?

increments.1: session 211: the cloth of 813 threads with its holes and knots, the light, the readout, one thread laid out, Sudan's written reason
increments.2: session 212: the rod (OCHA FTS funding share per thread, FEWS NET's lit or dark month from its own sitemap), re-hang by funding, pick out the dark months; critique committed
increments.3: session 213: the critique answered in the work: the dark months as a band through the cloth under a monitor strip, holes always bright, three hangs (time, country with names, what was given) each with its plain verdict, a close view for tapping, Sudan marked in the cloth, the months passing with sound
increments.4: session 214: the reader's hand: eighteen holes, one per country, each with its region's classified areas and its own past; a written phase darned into the cloth; the count of people the hand placed; a study (study.json, studio-unwoven-holes) offered through the house's frame; presented in presentations/cycle-011/

medium: An interactive canvas weave in the browser, with sound: one thread per IPC analysis and period, the areas' people in their phase colours, holes where people were written with no phase, a rod of funding and of the famine monitor's months above it.
embodies: WHAT THE RECORD WRITES FOR THE PLACES NO ONE COULD REACH. The IPC's open area table, Jan 2021 to Sep 2026: 60,652 area-periods in 813 threads; 1,041 holes holding 236,123,689 people counted once per period; 6,368 knots, places written with no people and no phase; one hole whose reason the IPC wrote.

atlas_neighbours.title: The Library of Missing Datasets
atlas_neighbours.daylight: There, data no one collects is an empty labelled folder. Here the record exists, names each blank and counts its people; what is missing is the one field the famine count turns on.

atlas_neighbours.title: The REDress Project
atlas_neighbours.daylight: There, an empty dress stands for a person a count leaves out. Here nothing stands in for anyone: the cloth is woven from the count itself, and the gap is the count's own.

atlas_neighbours.title: The Great Bare Mat and Constellation
atlas_neighbours.daylight: There, a carpet's pattern is plotted from the collective's traffic. Here the weave is the IPC's ledger at full scale, and the pattern that matters is where it is not woven.
